# Maahir Garg

> Maahir Garg is an AI Engineer with AICET's Team Koditsu and a Computer Science and Quantitative Finance student at the National University of Singapore, based in Singapore.

Current facts:

- AICET, Team Koditsu: AI Engineer since Aug 2026, researching model-based cheating-risk signals for coding assessments from character-level editor interaction streams and periodic code-state snapshots, with sequence-model and LLM approaches designed to support human review.
- GIC: AI Engineer from Jan to Jul 2026. Built an internal agentic CLI and sandboxed Chainlit assistant for an 11-person team with eight custom tools, multi-agent orchestration, skill routing, 50+ automated audit tests, separate custom evaluations, step-level guardrails, and Arize tracing. A Snowflake and SharePoint pipeline automated two manual data sources and reduced evidence retrieval from hours to near-instant.
- NUS teaching: currently teaches CS3230 Design and Analysis of Algorithms and CS3263 Foundations of Artificial Intelligence, leading a 21-student CS3230 tutorial. Across four teaching semesters and five appointments, earned a 4.8/5.0 teaching rating against a 4.2 faculty average and a place on the NUS Honour List of Student Tutors.
- Education: Bachelor of Computing (Honours) in Computer Science, Second Major in Quantitative Finance, Minor in Data Engineering, and specialisations in Artificial Intelligence with Distinction, Database Systems, and Computer Networks. GPA 4.71/5.00; expected graduation May 2027.
- Interactive 3D Lab: co-developed an iPhone and Apple Vision Pro tracking framework in collaboration with Apple for stroke-rehabilitation assessment, reaching 89% cross-device accuracy, 30 fps, and sub-millisecond latency. Co-author on a paper in preparation and co-inventor on a patent application in progress.
- Interests: photography, badminton, chess blitz, poker, swimming, and Formula 1.

Selected projects:

- PGPals: full-stack Next.js, TypeScript, and Supabase event platform supporting 164 authenticated users across 96 teams during a two-week residential challenge. It processed 2,297 submissions and 3,763 photo/video attachments across 103 challenges; enabled 78 multi-team pairings, 2,196 approved submissions, 2,289 credited team–challenge completions, and 46,540 PGP Coins awarded; and gave 10 administrators a 3.2-hour median review turnaround with zero submissions pending at event close. Public source: https://github.com/maahir-garg/pgpals
- Trader's Edge: team final-year project advised by Anand Bhojan, with a working MVP for plain-English strategy specification and historical-data backtesting. The demo requires Google sign-in. Public source is the NUS-FinTechAI team repository.
- Prediction-market engine: read-only FastAPI research engine over public Polymarket and Kalshi feeds, with human-confirmed pairings, fee and liquidity modelling, hedge-equal depth fills, and 36+ tests. It never places orders, holds funds, or reports realised P&L.
- BERT QA compression: 69% size reduction from 440 MB to 128 MB with no more than 0.5% F1 loss; custom mask-enforced pruning reached 54.7% sparsity.
- Domain-specific PEFT: BitFit updated no more than 0.1% of parameters, limited to bias terms, and improved reasoning accuracy from 47% to 73% on clause-extracted health-insurance scenarios.
